purpose: Formalize emergent distinctions and emergent invariants produced through interaction between localized orthogonal-transition branches.

core_principle.statement: An invariant is a distinction that remains preserved under changes in the mode of its actualization.
core_principle.interpretation: The concrete configuration may change while a specified structural relation remains preserved.

interaction.definition: Interaction is a process in which two or more localized process branches become mutually constraining or mutually informative and thereby alter the space of subsequently accessible distinctions.
interaction.principle: Interaction may generate properties not present as isolated properties of any single branch.

localization.definition: Localization is the formation of a distinguishable process or structure within a broader field of possible interactions.

emergent_distinction.definition: A distinction that becomes accessible through interaction and was not accessible in the same form within the isolated participating branches.
requirements: is not reducible to an unchanged isolated branch distinction
may become an input to subsequent processes
examples: new question generated by branch comparison

emergent_invariant.definition: A structural relation identified through interaction that remains preserved across relevant transformations or alternative actualizations.
requirements: identified from at least two distinguishable actualizations or transformations
not defined merely as an unchanged label
supports prediction or compression of subsequent observations
emergent_invariant.important_constraint: A candidate invariant is not an invariant merely because it was observed once.

invariant_detection.principle: An invariant is discovered by comparing transformations or alternative branch realizations, not by assuming it in advance.
procedure: compare candidate relation across branch realizations
retain as candidate invariant if preservation persists
reopen candidate if a counterexample appears

distinction_invariant_relation.principle: Emergent distinctions and emergent invariants are complementary outcomes of interaction.

invariant_as_new_axis.principle: Once an invariant is identified, it may itself become an axis relative to which new distinctions can be generated.
invariant_as_new_axis.consequence: Invariant discovery can expand rather than terminate the distinction space.
invariant_as_new_axis.important_constraint: An invariant is therefore not equivalent to process termination.

branch_comparison.principle: Branches may differ in local realization while sharing a structural invariant.

example.interpretation: A, B and C are non-identical actualizations preserving a common structural relation.

co_evolution.definition: Interaction may modify the accessible distinction space of more than one participating branch.
co_evolution.principle: A branch may discover a distinction through information generated by another branch rather than through isolated search.
co_evolution.consequence: Orthogonal-transition branches need not remain independent after localization.

counterexample.principle: A transformation that breaks a candidate invariant is evidence against its invariance within the tested domain.

does_not_claim: that every interaction produces an invariant
that every emergent distinction is an invariant
that every observed regularity is ontologically fundamental
that a candidate invariant is universally valid
that interaction necessarily produces physical structures

ufcps_invariants: Branch difference != absence of shared structure
OT branch diversity may increase invariant detectability

relation_to_orthogonal_transition.principle: Orthogonal transition creates alternative actualization regimes whose interaction can reveal distinctions and invariants unavailable from a single trajectory.
